doc: Ascent of a cyclone 1.01e-09 rad from the north pole (lon -2.9, age 1.3): its east vector cross(z, c) has norm 1.01e-09 (the sine of the colatitude), above the 1e-9 of the code, so the NORMAL east vector is used and the comma head shifts accordingly. Together the eight pole_colat_* cases (0.5, 0.9, 0.99, 0.99999 below; 1.00001, 1.01, 1.1, 2 above) pin the threshold 1e-9 to 1e-5 relative (the colatitude of a double latitude near pi/2 is itself quantized by 2.2e-16, i.e. 2.2e-7 relative, and the assertion that builds each case checks which side of 1e-9 the computed norm falls): a port with 1e-8, 1e-10 or 1.0001e-9 fails on at least one. 21 x 21 float32 patch of half-angle 0.5 rad. Measured on these eight patches: the float64-promoted computation differs by at most 1.2e-7 and a one-ulp nudge of the directions by 2.4e-7 (0.05 of the band). Conventions of cloudgen.sphere read here: lonlat_to_dir(lon, lat) = (cos lat cos lon, cos lat sin lon, sin lat) with float64 numpy cos and sin (right-handed, z north, longitude grows east; a vortex center is that direction); normalize(v) = v / |v| (plain division, no epsilon: a zero vector gives NaN). Tolerance rtol 5e-5, atol 5e-6: over the single-vortex float32 cases the float64-promoted computation differs by at most 3.1e-7 and a one-ulp nudge of the directions by 9e-7 (the oldest low, 0.44 of the default band); tolerance 10 times the worst, rounded up.

params.dtype_chain: p float32: a = float32 zeros; per vortex the center is cast to float32, d2, exp and the gaussians are float32 (a cyclone takes _comma_ascent, float32; a tropical subtracts its float32 eye); the term is np.float32(ascent) * g.astype(float32) and a += term accumulates in float32, in vortex order.
